audit_findings.title: Historical owner earnings may mix the divested Thermal Management perimeter with continuing operations
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inconsistent 2018–2022 OE observations affect the fitted log-trend anchor and the historical evidence supporting forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The Thermal Management business was previously disclosed as a stand-alone reporting segment, and is now presented as a discontinued operations in our Consolidated Financial Statements for all periods presented.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that Thermal Management is now discontinued, but the record does not establish whether the supplied pre-2023 OE observations came from unrecast filings. The error is therefore possible, not demonstrated. Its direction is indeterminate because changing different years can raise or lower the fitted endpoint, and no continuing-operations amounts are supplied for those years.
audit_findings.action: Trace each 2018–2022 OE observation to continuing-operations net income, depreciation, working capital and maintenance capital expenditure excluding Thermal Management; then rerun the trend or shorten the window if comparable data are unavailable.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may credit acquisition-funded earnings without charging acquisition reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,801.2 million of filed ECM, Trachte and Electrical Products Group purchase prices; computed growth-case sensitivity of $2,597 million–$3,663 million, or $15.64–$22.06 per share, above the 0% case
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings enter historical and anchor OE, while purchase prices are outside ordinary capital expenditures; applying 6%–8% growth without acquisition reinvestment can overstate projected OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used for investing activities from continuing operations was $1,063.7 million in 2025, which primarily related to cash paid for the Electrical Products Group acquisition of $979.6 million and capital expenditures of $93.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition outlays and their exclusion from ordinary capital expenditure are demonstrated. It remains unresolved whether the 6%–8% forecast is independently supportable by organic growth and reinvestment already deducted in OE. The issue is material because moving from the 0% case to the supplied growth cases accounts for $2.6–$3.7 billion of equity value.
audit_findings.action: Build an organic/acquired OE bridge for 2023–2026, calculate organic incremental OE against retained earnings and capital expenditure, and rerun growth using either organically supportable rates or a normalized acquisition-spending charge.

audit_findings.title: The 2023 OE observation may retain a material noncash tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $143.5 million potential combined net benefit; 28.7% of reported 2023 OE; if wholly retained, computed 2023 OE would be $356.8 million and the log-trend anchor approximately $509.8 million, 8.1% below $554.8 million
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax benefit retained in 2023 OE raises that observation and, through the log-trend regression, raises anchor OE and every scenario's operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2023, we recorded a non-cash income tax benefit of $ 93.2 million related to foreign income tax loss carryforwards resulting from tax-deductible statutory losses in Luxembourg.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate a $93.2 million Luxembourg benefit and a net $50.3 million Swiss benefit after the disclosed $5.1 million valuation allowance. Retention in OE is not demonstrated because the adjustment ledger is absent. If retained, the computed anchor effect is large enough to be valuation-material even though it would not close the gap to the $156.03 market price.
audit_findings.action: Produce the 2023 OE reconciliation and verify explicit removal of both tax benefits; if either remains, correct that observation and rerun the log trend and all valuation scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement obligations are a senior claim omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $130.8 million at December 31, 2025, equal to $0.79 per diluted share and 1.2%–1.9% of supplied scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded obligation not financed through projected OE should be deducted as a senior claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Pension and other post-retirement plan contributions totaled $ 5.4 million and $ 4.7 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The year-end funded deficit is a real existing claim, but deducting the full $130.8 million would reduce the supplied values by only about $0.79 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $156.03 price. Ongoing contributions of $5.4 million are already reflected in cash flow, so the bridge should avoid double counting.
audit_findings.action: Update the funded-status calculation to June 30, 2026 and document whether projected OE funds deficit-repair payments; deduct only the after-tax amount not already captured in OE.

audit_findings.title: Cash is added at face value despite repatriation constraints
audit_findings.magnitude: $79.6 million repatriation-constrained at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.48 per share; the entire $256.0 million cash bridge equals $1.54 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted, taxable-on-remittance or operating cash should be excluded or discounted before excess cash is added to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had $237.5 million of cash on hand, of which $72.7 million is held in certain countries in which the ability to repatriate is limited due to local regulations or significant potential tax consequences.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing identifies $79.6 million of constrained cash. Excluding all of it would lower value by only $0.48 per share; even excluding the entire $256.0 million cash balance would lower value by $1.54 per share. Neither scale changes the conclusion relative to the market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30 geographic cash schedule, calculate remittance taxes and legal restrictions, establish minimum operating cash, and replace the $256.0 million addition with verified distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset consumption may escape owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.0 million of 2025 finance-lease amortization and $17.8 million year-end finance-lease liability; the amortization is 0.2% of anchor OE and implies approximately $0.10 per share of base-case value if perpetually omitted
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding finance-lease amortization back through D&A without charging replacement capital or principal payments overstates recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We also have finance leases for production facilities and equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting risk is valid but small at the filed scale. The potentially omitted 2025 amortization is only $1.0 million versus $554.8 million of anchor OE; even treating it as a permanent missing charge changes base value by approximately $0.10 per share. The $17.8 million liability is likewise about $0.11 per share if treated as a bridge claim.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile D&A add-backs to finance-lease amortization, confirm whether lease principal or replacement capital is charged in OE, and obtain the June 30, 2026 finance-lease asset and liability balances.
